name: Mountain Lion
description: Solitary apex predator intelligence spanning the largest range of any terrestrial mammal in the Western Hemisphere. Masters ambush predation through terrain-reading and concealment calculus — selecting attack positions that minimize detection probability while maximizing strike success. Maintains vast territories (up to 1,000 km2) through scent-marking boundary protocols. Crepuscular activity patterns exploit prey vulnerability windows at dawn and dusk.

core_attributes.pattern: ambush predation, territory management, crepuscular timing

scope.definition: Optimal launch-point selection efficiency — measured as ratio of actual energy expended in mountain lion ambush attacks to minimum theoretical energy for equivalent prey capture on same terrain.

evidence.source: Elbroch & Wittmer (2012) 'Puma predatory behaviour in the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem', Journal of Zoology 286:264-270; Laundré et al. (2001) 'Wolves, elk, and bison' Oikos 95:297-310.
cross_domain_examples: GPS-tracked mountain lions select ambush sites reducing stalk energy by 35-50% vs random sites
optimal approach uses terrain occlusion: 89% of successful attacks initiated from ridge/rock cover
tiger ambush site selection: same opportunistic use of terrain features for energy-minimizing predation

scope.falsifiability: If GPS data shows mountain lion attack launch points are randomly distributed relative to terrain features, rather than concentrated at occlusion and height advantage locations, deliberate site selection is not occurring.
scope.measurement_limits: Ambush optimization is prey-type dependent — deer vs elk ambush geometry differs. Nocturnal ambush (primary strategy) is harder to study; most data comes from track analysis and GPS kill-site clustering.

scope.definition: Precision of territory boundary maintenance — fraction of GPS-tracked mountain lion locations within previously established territory boundaries, measured as boundary permeability index across seasonal cycles.

evidence.source: Beier et al. (1995) 'Mountain lion predation in southern California', Ecological Monographs 65:367-385; Robinson et al. (2014) 'Sink populations in carnivore management', Ecological Applications.
cross_domain_examples: GPS collared mountain lions maintain 78-94% of relocations within core territory across 12-month periods
territory scent marking increases to 3× baseline at boundary zones — active maintenance investment
wolf territory maintenance: analogous boundary reinforcement with howling and scent marking

scope.falsifiability: If GPS relocation data shows mountain lion movement random with respect to prior territory boundaries (no clustering inside boundary), territory maintenance is not an active behavioral strategy.
scope.measurement_limits: Territory boundary precision decreases with prey migration (lions follow prey across nominal boundaries). Sub-adult lions have undefined territories with highly variable movement patterns.

scope.definition: Proportion of mountain lion prey captures occurring within 2 hours of dawn or dusk (crepuscular window) vs equivalent activity by prey species — measured by GPS kill-site timestamps.

evidence.source: Boydston et al. (2003) 'Sex differences in cougar use of and vulnerability of mule deer', Behavioral Ecology 14:698-704; Laundré (2010) 'Behavioral response races: stealth versus flesh', Oecologia.
cross_domain_examples: 66-78% of mountain lion prey kills occur during crepuscular 4-hour window (2h dawn + 2h dusk)
crepuscular kill rate 3× higher per hour vs midday hours — visual advantage maximized
ambush spider Mastophora activity peaks at dusk: analogous timing optimization using prey circadian pattern

scope.falsifiability: If kills are uniformly distributed across 24 hours with no crepuscular peak in GPS data across 100+ documented kills, crepuscular timing is not a deliberate strategy.
scope.measurement_limits: Crepuscular activity increases when prey density is high (less stalking needed per kill) and during winter (prey more concentrated). Human disturbance shifts lions to nocturnal activity in suburban interface zones.
